rejection_summary: Dimensions (2011, tt1703231): scientist/time-travel premise is substantially relationship and period-drama driven; whole-runtime evidence describes it as slow and emotionally focused, with insufficient sustained investigation and rule discovery for the 82 baseline threshold.

The Atomic Man / Timeslip (1955, tt0048964): strong opening anomaly and investigative first half, but substantive reception says the seven-second time displacement premise is underused as the plot shifts into industrial espionage, sabotage and gangster mechanics; insufficient sustained concept/rule escalation.

The Strange World of Planet X (1958, tt0051020): scientists and dangerous magnetic-field experiments are central early, but the consequences resolve into giant-insect/monster threat, military intervention and an alien warning rather than sustained scientific discovery; fails the profile's creature/action guardrail intent.
